title: Friends
tagline: Roadside Tong-er Cha, Weekend Cycling, Books & Life Beyond Code
description: Get to know me outside the terminal — tea sessions, Sajek adventures, cycling trails, reading books & heartfelt addas.
about: Hey there! I'm Nokib, based in Dhaka, Bangladesh. Beyond debugging code and building web apps, I'm all about roadside hot lemon tea, evening addas with close friends, mountain treks to Sajek & Bandarban, early morning cycling, and getting lost in good books. I believe life's best memories happen off-screen over great conversations and a warm cup of tea.

voiceNote.transcript: Hey! Thanks for stopping by this corner of the site. Resumes and portfolios can feel way too formal, so I made this friend space. If you're ever in Dhaka, let's grab some Tong-er cha or coffee. Always down for travel stories, cycling trails, book exchanges, and casual chats.

timeline.title: Trekking Above Clouds in Sajek Valley
timeline.description: A week-long adventure through the peaks of Sajek, sitting on helipads under starry night skies and sipping hillside tea.
timeline.story:
There is a surreal feeling when you wake up at 5:00 AM on the hills of Ruilui Para in Sajek. The entire valley below is enveloped in a sea of thick white clouds, while the sun slowly paints the mountain silhouettes in orange and gold.

We spent days exploring the winding hilly roads on foot, sitting on the army helipad at midnight counting shooting stars, and having endless conversations over roadside ginger tea. It was a reminder of why stepping away from the keyboard is essential to recharge one's creativity and soul.

timeline.title: Long-Distance Cycling & Trail Discovery
timeline.description: Started regular 30km+ early morning cycling routes through quiet Dhaka bridges, riverbanks, and countryside lanes.
timeline.story:
Dhaka during the day is loud, buzzing, and full of chaotic energy. But at 5:30 AM on a Friday, the city transforms into something magical.

I bought my hybrid road bike and started riding along the quiet Hatirjheel waterfront, crossing the 300 Feet expressway, and pushing deep into the green rural outskirts towards the Balu river. Cycling taught me rhythm, endurance, and the joy of exploring the world at 20 kilometers per hour.

timeline.title: Deep Dive into Books & Philosophy
timeline.description: Built a personal library of non-fiction, philosophy, and tech essays. Discovering how timeless ideas shape our modern world.
timeline.story:
During the stillness of 2020, I started devouring books on human history, philosophy, and timeless design principles. From Marcus Aurelius' Meditations to Haruki Murakami's novels and classic software architecture essays, reading became my daily meditation.

I realized that code is just a medium to express thought; understanding human philosophy is what actually helps us build meaningful software and live fulfilling lives.

timeline.title: Bandarban Road Trip with Friends
timeline.description: Open-hood Chander Gari rides through Nilgiri hills, hiking down to Nafakhum falls, and eating steaming hot roadside khichuri in monsoon rain.
timeline.story:
Nothing bonds friends quite like an unpredictable monsoon trip to the remote hills of Bandarban. Standing on the roof of a Chander Gari as it climbed steep winding roads through dense green clouds was pure adrenaline.

We hiked 4 hours across rocky streams to reach the roaring Nafakhum waterfall, completely disconnected from mobile networks, Wi-Fi, and deadlines. We ate steaming hot roadside khichuri with dim bhaji under tin roofs listening to the monsoon rain.

timeline.title: The Very First 'Hello World' Moment
timeline.description: Fired up an old desktop and wrote my first HTML & C programs. Seeing the black terminal respond sparked a spark that redefined everything.
timeline.story:
It all started in a small room on an old clunky desktop computer. I typed my first lines of C code and clicked compile. When the black terminal window popped up with `Hello, World!`, something clicked in my brain.

The realization that you could type English words and logical instructions to make a machine solve complex problems, build interactive screens, and connect with people across the globe felt like actual magic. That curiosity has fueled everything I build today.
